/**
 * Locator Abstraction Layer
 *
 * This module provides a unified API for locating and interacting with DOM elements
 * that works in both browser mode (Playwright) and Happy-DOM environments.
 *
 * Environment detection:
 * - Browser mode: Uses vitest-browser-vue native page object and userEvent
 * - Happy-DOM: Uses @testing-library/vue screen queries and user-event
 *
 * Usage:
 * - Import `page` for querying elements
 * - Import `userEvent` for user interactions
 * - Import type `Locator` and `Page` for type annotations
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * import { page, userEvent, type Locator } from '@/__tests__/helpers/locator'
 *
 * const button = page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Submit' })
 * await button.click()
 * ```
 */

import type { Page } from './types'

/**
 * Detect if we're running in Vitest browser mode.
 * In browser mode, window.__vitest_browser__ is set by Vitest.
 */
const isBrowserMode =
  globalThis.window !== undefined && '__vitest_browser__' in globalThis

// Use top-level await with dynamic import to load the correct implementation
// This works in ESM environments (both Node and browser)
const impl = isBrowserMode
  ? await import('./browser')
  : await import('./happy-dom')

/**
 * Page object for querying elements.
 * Automatically uses the correct implementation based on environment.
 */
export const page: Page = impl.page

/**
 * User event for simulating user interactions.
 * Automatically uses the correct implementation based on environment.
 */
export const userEvent = impl.userEvent

// Re-export types
export type {
  Locator,
  Page,
  ARIARole,
  LocatorOptions,
  LocatorByRoleOptions,
  LocatorSelectors,
  UserEventClickOptions,
  UserEventFillOptions,
  UserEventClearOptions,
  UserEventHoverOptions,
  UserEventSelectOptions,
} from './types'

   111→  }
   112→
   113→  return elements.filter((el) => {
   114→    const text = el.textContent ?? ''
   115→
   116→    if (options.hasText && !textMatches(text, options.hasText)) {
   117→      return false
   118→    }
   119→
   120→    if (options.hasNotText && textMatches(text, options.hasNotText)) {
   121→      return false
   122→    }
   123→
   124→    return true
   125→  })
   126→}
   127→
   128→/**
   129→ * Filter elements based on has/hasNot locator options
   130→ */
   131→function filterByLocator(elements: Array<HTMLElement>, options?: LocatorOptions): Array<HTMLElement> {
   132→  if (!options) {
   133→    return elements
   134→  }
   135→
   136→  return elements.filter((el) => {
   137→    if (options.has && isHappyDomLocator(options.has)) {
   138→      // Element must contain a match for the 'has' locator
   139→      const hasMatch = options.has.queryWithin(el)
   140→      if (!hasMatch) return false
   141→    }
   142→
   143→    if (options.hasNot && isHappyDomLocator(options.hasNot)) {
   144→      // Element must NOT contain a match for the 'hasNot' locator
   145→      const hasNotMatch = options.hasNot.queryWithin(el)
   146→      if (hasNotMatch) return false
   147→    }
   148→
   149→    return true
   150→  })
   151→}
   152→
   153→/**
   154→ * Apply all filters to elements
   155→ */
   156→function applyFilters(elements: Array<HTMLElement>, options?: LocatorOptions): Array<HTMLElement> {
   157→  let result = elements
   158→  result = filterByText(result, options)
   159→  result = filterByLocator(result, options)
   160→  return result
   161→}
   162→
   163→/**
   164→ * Safely cast array of Elements to HTMLElement array using filter
   165→ */
   166→function toHTMLElements(elements: Array<Element>): Array<HTMLElement> {
   167→  return elements.filter(isHTMLElement)
   168→}
   169→
   170→/**
   171→ * Extract HTMLElement from a locator's element() result
   172→ */
   173→function getHTMLElementFromLocator(locator: HappyDomLocator): HTMLElement {
   174→  const el = locator.element()
   175→  if (!isHTMLElement(el)) {
   176→    throw new Error('Expected HTMLElement from locator')
   177→  }
   178→  return el
   179→}
   180→
   181→/**
   182→ * Convert select values to user-event format
   183→ */
   184→function convertSelectValues(
   185→  values: HTMLElement | HTMLElement[] | Locator | Locator[] | string | string[],
   186→): HTMLElement | HTMLElement[] | string | string[] {
   187→  // Handle single Locator
   188→  if (isHappyDomLocator(values)) {
   189→    return getHTMLElementFromLocator(values)
   190→  }
   191→
   192→  // Handle single HTMLElement
   193→  if (isHTMLElement(values)) {
   194→    return values
   195→  }
   196→
   197→  // Handle string
   198→  if (isString(values)) {
   199→    return values
   200→  }
   201→
   202→  // Handle arrays - need to process each element
   203→  if (!Array.isArray(values)) {
   204→    // This shouldn't happen given the type, but TypeScript needs it
   205→    throw new TypeError('Unexpected value type for selectOptions')
   206→  }
   207→
   208→  return convertArrayValues(values)
   209→}
   210→
   211→/**
   212→ * Convert array of select values
   213→ */
   214→function convertArrayValues(
   215→  values: Array<HTMLElement | Locator | string>,
   216→): HTMLElement[] | string[] {
   217→  const firstValue = values[0]
   218→  if (firstValue === undefined) {
   219→    return []
   220→  }
   221→
   222→  // Check if array contains locators
   223→  if (isHappyDomLocator(firstValue)) {
   224→    return extractLocatorElements(values)
   225→  }
   226→
   227→  // Check if array contains HTMLElements
   228→  if (isHTMLElement(firstValue)) {
   229→    return extractHTMLElements(values)
   230→  }
   231→
   232→  // Must be strings
   233→  if (isString(firstValue)) {
   234→    return extractStrings(values)
   235→  }
   236→
   237→  throw new Error('Unexpected array element type for selectOptions')
   238→}
   239→
   240→function extractLocatorElements(values: Array<HTMLElement | Locator | string>): Array<HTMLElement> {
   241→  const result: Array<HTMLElement> = []
   242→  for (const v of values) {
   243→    if (isHappyDomLocator(v)) {
   244→      result.push(getHTMLElementFromLocator(v))
   245→    }
   246→  }
   247→  return result
   248→}
   249→
   250→function extractHTMLElements(values: Array<HTMLElement | Locator | string>): Array<HTMLElement> {
   251→  const result: Array<HTMLElement> = []
   252→  for (const v of values) {
   253→    if (isHTMLElement(v)) {
   254→      result.push(v)
   255→    }
   256→  }
   257→  return result
   258→}
   259→
   260→function extractStrings(values: Array<HTMLElement | Locator | string>): Array<string> {
   261→  const result: Array<string> = []
   262→  for (const v of values) {
   263→    if (isString(v)) {
   264→      result.push(v)
   265→    }
   266→  }
   267→  return result
   268→}

   270→/**
   271→ * Mapping of ARIA roles to their implicit HTML element selectors.
   272→ * HTML elements have implicit ARIA roles that don't require explicit role attributes.
   273→ * @see https://www.w3.org/TR/html-aria/#docconformance
   274→ */
   275→const IMPLICIT_ROLE_SELECTORS: Record<string, string> = {
   276→  // Table roles
   277→  table: 'table',
   278→  row: 'tr',
   279→  cell: 'td',
   280→  columnheader: 'th',
   281→  rowheader: 'th[scope="row"]',
   282→  rowgroup: 'tbody, thead, tfoot',
   283→  // Form roles
   284→  button: 'button, input[type="button"], input[type="submit"], input[type="reset"], input[type="image"]',
   285→  checkbox: 'input[type="checkbox"]',
   286→  radio: 'input[type="radio"]',
   287→  textbox: 'input:not([type]), input[type="text"], input[type="email"], input[type="tel"], input[type="url"], input[type="search"], input[type="password"], textarea',
   288→  spinbutton: 'input[type="number"]',
   289→  combobox: 'select:not([multiple]):not([size]), select[size="1"]',
   290→  listbox: 'select[multiple], select[size]:not([size="1"])',
   291→  slider: 'input[type="range"]',
   292→  option: 'option',
   293→  // Landmark roles
   294→  main: 'main',
   295→  navigation: 'nav',
   296→  banner: 'header:not(article header, section header)',
   297→  contentinfo: 'footer:not(article footer, section footer)',
   298→  complementary: 'aside',
   299→  form: 'form[aria-label], form[aria-labelledby], form[name]',
   300→  region: 'section[aria-label], section[aria-labelledby]',
   301→  search: 'search',
   302→  // Document structure roles
   303→  article: 'article',
   304→  heading: 'h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6',
   305→  list: 'ul, ol',
   306→  listitem: 'li',
   307→  link: 'a[href]',
   308→  img: 'img[alt]:not([alt=""])',
   309→  figure: 'figure',
   310→  separator: 'hr',
   311→  // Widget roles
   312→  dialog: '[role="dialog"], dialog',
   313→  tab: '[role="tab"]',
   314→  tablist: '[role="tablist"]',
   315→  tabpanel: '[role="tabpanel"]',
   316→  menu: '[role="menu"]',
   317→  menuitem: '[role="menuitem"]',
   318→  menuitemcheckbox: '[role="menuitemcheckbox"]',
   319→  menuitemradio: '[role="menuitemradio"]',
   320→  progressbar: 'progress',
   321→  status: 'output',
   322→  alert: '[role="alert"]',
   323→  alertdialog: '[role="alertdialog"]',
   324→  tooltip: '[role="tooltip"]',
   325→  tree: '[role="tree"]',
   326→  treeitem: '[role="treeitem"]',
   327→  grid: '[role="grid"]',
   328→  gridcell: '[role="gridcell"]',
   329→}
   330→
   331→/**
   332→ * Build a CSS selector for a given ARIA role that includes both explicit and implicit matches.
   333→ */
   334→function buildRoleSelector(role: string): string {
   335→  const explicitSelector = `[role="${role}"]`
   336→  const implicitSelector = IMPLICIT_ROLE_SELECTORS[role]
   337→
   338→  if (implicitSelector) {
   339→    return `${explicitSelector}, ${implicitSelector}`
   340→  }
   341→  return explicitSelector
   342→}
   343→
   344→/**
   345→ * Get the accessible name from aria-labelledby attribute.
   346→ */
   347→function getNameFromLabelledBy(element: HTMLElement): string | null {
   348→  const labelledBy = element.getAttribute('aria-labelledby')
   349→  if (!labelledBy) return null
   350→
   351→  const labelIds = labelledBy.split(/\s+/)
   352→  const labelTexts: Array<string> = []
   353→  for (const id of labelIds) {
   354→    const labelElement = document.querySelector(`#${id}`)
   355→    if (labelElement) {
   356→      labelTexts.push(labelElement.textContent?.trim() ?? '')
   357→    }
   358→  }
   359→  const combinedLabel = labelTexts.join(' ').trim()
   360→  return combinedLabel || null
   361→}
   362→
   363→/**
   364→ * Get the accessible name from associated label element.
   365→ */
   366→function getNameFromAssociatedLabel(element: HTMLElement): string | null {
   367→  if (!(element instanceof HTMLInputElement || element instanceof HTMLTextAreaElement || element instanceof HTMLSelectElement)) {
   368→    return null
   369→  }
   370→  const { id } = element
   371→  if (!id) return null
   372→
   373→  const label = document.querySelector<HTMLLabelElement>(`label[for="${id}"]`)
   374→  return label?.textContent?.trim() ?? null
   375→}
   376→
   377→/**
   378→ * Get the accessible name of an element.
   379→ * Checks aria-label, aria-labelledby, and falls back to text content.
   380→ * @see https://www.w3.org/TR/accname-1.1/
   381→ */
   382→function getAccessibleName(element: HTMLElement): string {
   383→  // 1. Check aria-label attribute
   384→  const ariaLabel = element.getAttribute('aria-label')
   385→  if (ariaLabel) return ariaLabel.trim()
   386→
   387→  // 2. Check aria-labelledby attribute
   388→  const labelledByName = getNameFromLabelledBy(element)
   389→  if (labelledByName) return labelledByName
   390→
   391→  // 3. For form elements, check associated label
   392→  const associatedLabel = getNameFromAssociatedLabel(element)
   393→  if (associatedLabel) return associatedLabel
   394→
   395→  // 4. Fall back to text content for buttons, links, etc.
   396→  return element.textContent?.trim() ?? ''
   397→}
   398→
   399→/**
   400→ * Filter elements by accessible name.
   401→ */
   402→function filterByAccessibleName(elements: Array<HTMLElement>, namePattern: string | RegExp | undefined): Array<HTMLElement> {
   403→  if (namePattern === undefined) {
   404→    return elements
   405→  }
   406→
   407→  return elements.filter((el) => {
   408→    const accessibleName = getAccessibleName(el)
   409→    return textMatches(accessibleName, namePattern)
   410→  })
   411→}
   412→
   413→/**
   414→ * Filter out elements that have an explicit role attribute different from the target role.
   415→ * This ensures that implicit role matching (e.g., input[type="text"] matching "textbox")
   416→ * doesn't match elements with an explicit role override (e.g., role="spinbutton").
   417→ */
   418→function filterByExplicitRole(elements: Array<HTMLElement>, targetRole: string): Array<HTMLElement> {
   419→  return elements.filter((el) => {
   420→    const explicitRole = el.getAttribute('role')
   421→    // If no explicit role, the implicit role applies - keep the element
   422→    if (!explicitRole) return true
   423→    // If explicit role matches target, keep it
   424→    if (explicitRole === targetRole) return true
   425→    // Explicit role differs from target - exclude this element
   426→    return false
   427→  })
   428→}
   429→
   430→/**
   431→ * Create a scoped query function for getByRole within parent elements
   432→ */
   433→function createScopedRoleQuery(
   434→  parentQueryFn: () => Array<HTMLElement>,
   435→  role: ARIARole | (string & {}),
   436→  options?: LocatorByRoleOptions,
   437→): () => Array<HTMLElement> {
   438→  return () => {
   439→    const parentElements = parentQueryFn()
   440→    const results: Array<HTMLElement> = []
   441→    const selector = buildRoleSelector(role)
   442→    for (const parentEl of parentElements) {
   443→      const els = parentEl.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>(selector)
   444→      for (const el of els) {
   445→        results.push(el)
   446→      }
   447→    }
   448→    // Filter out elements with explicit roles that differ from the target role
   449→    const filteredByExplicitRole = filterByExplicitRole(results, role)
   450→    // Filter by accessible name if provided
   451→    const filteredByName = filterByAccessibleName(filteredByExplicitRole, options?.name)
   452→    return applyFilters(filteredByName, options)
   453→  }
   454→}

   456→/**
   457→ * Create a scoped query function for getByLabelText within parent elements
   458→ */
   459→function createScopedLabelTextQuery(
   460→  parentQueryFn: () => Array<HTMLElement>,
   461→  text: string | RegExp,
   462→  options?: LocatorOptions,
   463→): () => Array<HTMLElement> {

   465→    const parentElements = parentQueryFn()
   466→    const results: Array<HTMLElement> = []
   467→    for (const parentEl of parentElements) {
   468→      const labels = parentEl.querySelectorAll<HTMLLabelElement>('label')
   469→      for (const label of labels) {
   470→        const labelText = label.textContent ?? ''
   471→        const matches = textMatches(labelText, text, options?.exact)
   472→        if (matches && label.htmlFor) {
   473→          const input = parentEl.querySelector<HTMLElement>(`#${label.htmlFor}`)
   474→          if (input) results.push(input)
   475→        }
   476→      }
   477→    }
   478→    return applyFilters(results, options)
   479→  }

   528→/**
   529→ * Create a scoped query function for getByText within parent elements
   530→ */
   531→function createScopedTextQuery(
   532→  parentQueryFn: () => Array<HTMLElement>,
   533→  text: string | RegExp,
   534→  options?: LocatorOptions,
   535→): () => Array<HTMLElement> {
   536→  return () => {
   537→    const parentElements = parentQueryFn()
   538→    const results: Array<HTMLElement> = []
   539→    for (const parentEl of parentElements) {
   540→      const walker = document.createTreeWalker(parentEl, NodeFilter.SHOW_TEXT)
   541→      let node: Node | null
   542→      while ((node = walker.nextNode())) {
   543→        const nodeText = node.textContent ?? ''
   544→        const textToMatch = options?.exact ? nodeText.trim() : nodeText
   545→        const matches = textMatches(textToMatch, text, options?.exact)
   546→        if (matches && node.parentElement) {
   547→          results.push(node.parentElement)
   548→        }
   549→      }
   550→    }
   551→    return applyFilters(results, options)
   552→  }

   600→/**

   602→ */
   603→function createNthQuery(parentQueryFn: () => Array<HTMLElement>, index: number): () => Array<HTMLElement> {
   604→  return () => {
   605→    const elements = parentQueryFn()
   606→    return elements[index] ? [elements[index]] : []
   607→  }
   608→}
   609→
   610→/**
   611→ * Create a last query function
   612→ */
   613→function createLastQuery(parentQueryFn: () => Array<HTMLElement>): () => Array<HTMLElement> {
   614→  return () => {
   615→    const elements = parentQueryFn()
   616→    return elements.length > 0 ? [elements.at(-1)!] : []
   617→  }

   619→
   620→/**
   621→ * Create an 'and' query function
   622→ */
   623→function createAndQuery(
   624→  queryFn1: () => Array<HTMLElement>,
   625→  queryFn2: () => Array<HTMLElement>,
   626→): () => Array<HTMLElement> {
   627→  return () => {
   628→    const thisElements = new Set(queryFn1())
   629→    const otherElements = queryFn2()
   630→    return otherElements.filter((el) => thisElements.has(el))
   631→  }
   632→}
   633→
   634→/**
   635→ * Create an 'or' query function
   636→ */
   637→function createOrQuery(
   638→  queryFn1: () => Array<HTMLElement>,
   639→  queryFn2: () => Array<HTMLElement>,
   640→): () => Array<HTMLElement> {
   641→  return () => {
   642→    const thisElements = queryFn1()
   643→    const otherElements = queryFn2()
   644→    const combined = new Map<HTMLElement, true>()
   645→    for (const el of thisElements) combined.set(el, true)
   646→    for (const el of otherElements) combined.set(el, true)
   647→    return [...combined.keys()]
   648→  }
   649→}

   651→/**
   652→ * Create a filter query function
   653→ */
   654→function createFilterQuery(
   655→  parentQueryFn: () => Array<HTMLElement>,
   656→  options: LocatorOptions,
   657→): () => Array<HTMLElement> {
   658→  return () => {
   659→    const elements = parentQueryFn()
   660→    return applyFilters(elements, options)
   661→  }
   662→}

   664→/**
   665→ * Happy-DOM implementation of the Locator interface.
   666→ * Uses @testing-library for queries and user-event for interactions.
   667→ */
   668→class HappyDomLocator implements Locator {
   669→  private readonly queryFn: () => Array<HTMLElement>
   670→  private readonly selectorStr: string
   671→
   672→  constructor(queryFn: () => Array<HTMLElement>, selector: string) {
   673→    this.queryFn = queryFn

   678→    return this.selectorStr
   679→  }

   681→  /**
   682→   * Query for elements within a specific container (used by has/hasNot)
   683→   */
   684→  queryWithin(container: HTMLElement): HTMLElement | null {
   685→    const allElements = this.queryFn()
   686→    return allElements.find((el) => container.contains(el)) ?? null

   696→  }

   716→    )
   717→  }
   718→
   719→  getByText(text: string | RegExp, options?: LocatorOptions): Locator {

   722→      `${this.selectorStr} >> text=${String(text)}`,

   724→  }

I see the test fails even when running individually. The key issue is that the DOM shows an empty "Workout Plan" state - the block wasn't added.

Let me add debug output to understand where the failure happens. First, let me compare the passing test #1 with the failing test #3.

Test #1 (passes):
```ts
await builder.navigateTo()
await builder.openAddBlockDialog()
// Switch to timed blocks tab
await builder.switchToTimedBlocksTab()
// Verify all block types are available
await expectElement(page.getByText('AMRAP')).toBeInTheDocument()
// Select AMRAP
await userEvent.click(common.getDialogButton('AMRAP'))
// Wait for configuration dialog
await expectElement(page.getByRole('dialog')).toBeVisible()
await expectElement(page.getByText(/Configure/)).toBeVisible()
// Add an exercise to the AMRAP
await userEvent.click(common.getDialogButton('Add Exercise'))
await common.selectExercise('Push-ups')
// Confirm the block
await userEvent.click(common.getDialogButton('Add Block'))
// Wait for dialog AND overlay to fully close
await common.waitForDialogClose()
```

Test #3 (fails) - uses `builder.addTimedBlock('AMRAP')`:
```ts
await this.openAddBlockDialog()
await this.switchToTimedBlocksTab()
// Wait for block type buttons to be visible after tab switch
await expectElement(page.getByText(blockType, { exact: true })).toBeVisible()
await userEvent.click(this.common.getDialogButton(blockType))
// Wait for configure dialog
await expectElement(page.getByText('Configure')).toBeVisible()
// Add exercise
const exerciseButtonText = blockType === 'Tabata' ? 'Select Exercise' : 'Add Exercise'
await userEvent.click(this.common.getDialogButton(exerciseButtonText))
await this.common.selectExercise(exerciseName)
// Confirm block
await userEvent.click(this.common.getDialogButton('Add Block'))
await this.common.waitForDialogClose()
```

The differences are subtle:
1. Test #1: `await expectElement(page.getByText('AMRAP')).toBeInTheDocument()`
   addTimedBlock: `await expectElement(page.getByText(blockType, { exact: true })).toBeVisible()`

2. Test #1: `await expectElement(page.getByText(/Configure/)).toBeVisible()`
   addTimedBlock: `await expectElement(page.getByText('Configure')).toBeVisible()`

The second difference could be important - Test #1 uses regex `/Configure/` while `addTimedBlock` uses exact string `'Configure'`. The actual text might be "Configure AMRAP" not just "Configure".

So the dialog title is "Configure AMRAP", not "Configure". The test `addTimedBlock` uses `await expectElement(page.getByText('Configure')).toBeVisible()` which should still match because `getByText('Configure')` does substring matching by default (not exact match).

Wait, let me re-check. Looking at the happy-dom implementation:

```ts
function textMatches(text: string, pattern: string | RegExp, exact?: boolean): boolean {
  if (typeof pattern === 'string') {
    return exact ? text === pattern : text.includes(pattern)
  }
  return pattern.test(text)
}
```

So `getByText('Configure')` without `exact: true` should match "Configure AMRAP" because it uses `includes()`. That should work.

Let me check if there's something wrong with clicking the button. Let me look at the previous fix that addressed similar issues:

Interesting - the test still fails even when run with the pattern `-t "Execution > creates AMRAP block"`. This means it's not related to test ordering.

Notice that even when I try to run only that test, the two Configuration tests still run and pass first. This is because vitest pattern matching uses `includes` - it runs all tests in the file that contain that pattern.

Let me look at the key difference between the working Test #1 "allows user to add timed blocks..." and the failing Test #3 "creates AMRAP block...":

Test #1 does these steps manually:
```ts
await builder.navigateTo()
await builder.openAddBlockDialog()
await builder.switchToTimedBlocksTab()
await expectElement(page.getByText('AMRAP')).toBeInTheDocument()
await userEvent.click(common.getDialogButton('AMRAP'))
await expectElement(page.getByRole('dialog')).toBeVisible()
await expectElement(page.getByText(/Configure/)).toBeVisible()
await userEvent.click(common.getDialogButton('Add Exercise'))
await common.selectExercise('Push-ups')
await userEvent.click(common.getDialogButton('Add Block'))
await common.waitForDialogClose()
```

Test #3 uses the helper:
```ts
await builder.navigateTo()
await builder.addTimedBlock('AMRAP')  // This is the helper method
```

Where `addTimedBlock` does:
```ts
await this.openAddBlockDialog()
await this.switchToTimedBlocksTab()
await expectElement(page.getByText(blockType, { exact: true })).toBeVisible()
await userEvent.click(this.common.getDialogButton(blockType))
await expectElement(page.getByText('Configure')).toBeVisible()
const exerciseButtonText = 'Add Exercise'  // for AMRAP
await userEvent.click(this.common.getDialogButton(exerciseButtonText))
await this.common.selectExercise(exerciseName)
await userEvent.click(this.common.getDialogButton('Add Block'))
await this.common.waitForDialogClose()
```

The differences:
1. Test #1 uses `page.getByText('AMRAP')` (no exact option)
   Helper uses `page.getByText(blockType, { exact: true })` (exact: true)

2. Test #1 uses `page.getByText(/Configure/)` (regex)
   Helper uses `page.getByText('Configure')` (string, no regex)

3. Test #1 has an extra `await expectElement(page.getByRole('dialog')).toBeVisible()` before checking Configure text

Let me check the `exact: true` option. Looking at happy-dom.ts line 85-93:
```ts
function toQueryOptions(options?: LocatorOptions): { exact?: boolean } | undefined {
  if (!options) {
    return undefined
  }
  return {
    exact: options.exact,
  }
}
```

And in `getByText` at line 930:
```ts
getByText(text: string | RegExp, options?: LocatorOptions): Locator {
  return new HappyDomLocator(() => {
    try {
      const els = screen.queryAllByText(text, toQueryOptions(options))
      return applyFilters(toHTMLElements(els), options)
    } catch {
      return []
    }
  }, `text=${String(text)}`)
}
```

With `{ exact: true }`, `screen.queryAllByText('AMRAP', { exact: true })` would only match elements whose text content is exactly "AMRAP", not elements containing "AMRAP" in a larger string.

But the AMRAP button has text content like "AMRAP As Many Rounds As Possible in a set time ›". With `exact: true`, this wouldn't match!

That's the bug! The `addTimedBlock` method uses `{ exact: true }` which causes the wait to fail because the button text isn't exactly "AMRAP" - it's "AMRAP" plus the description.

Let me verify by checking what `screen.queryAllByText` does with `exact: true`:

Actually, looking at the testing-library docs, `exact: true` makes the match exact for the text content. So `queryAllByText('AMRAP', { exact: true })` would NOT match an element with text "AMRAP As Many Rounds As Possible...".

Let me check if this is indeed the issue:

Actually, let me take a different approach. Let me look at how the first passing test differs from the failing one at a deeper level. Let me compare the exact sequences:

**Test #1 (passes)**:
```ts
await builder.navigateTo()
await builder.openAddBlockDialog()
// At this point: dialog is open, Exercises tab is active

await builder.switchToTimedBlocksTab()
// At this point: Timed Blocks tab is active

await expectElement(page.getByText('AMRAP')).toBeInTheDocument()
// Verify AMRAP text is in the document

await userEvent.click(common.getDialogButton('AMRAP'))
// Click the AMRAP button

await expectElement(page.getByRole('dialog')).toBeVisible()  // EXTRA WAIT
await expectElement(page.getByText(/Configure/)).toBeVisible()
// Wait for configure dialog

await userEvent.click(common.getDialogButton('Add Exercise'))
await common.selectExercise('Push-ups')
await userEvent.click(common.getDialogButton('Add Block'))
await common.waitForDialogClose()
```

**`addTimedBlock` helper**:
```ts
await this.openAddBlockDialog()
// Dialog is open, Exercises tab is active

await this.switchToTimedBlocksTab()
// Timed Blocks tab is active

await expectElement(page.getByText(blockType, { exact: true })).toBeVisible()
// Wait for AMRAP to be visible

await userEvent.click(this.common.getDialogButton(blockType))
// Click the AMRAP button

await expectElement(page.getByText('Configure')).toBeVisible()  // NO EXTRA WAIT FOR DIALOG
// Wait for configure dialog text

await userEvent.click(this.common.getDialogButton(exerciseButtonText))
await this.common.selectExercise(exerciseName)
await userEvent.click(this.common.getDialogButton('Add Block'))
await this.common.waitForDialogClose()
```

The key difference I see is:
- Test #1 has an extra `await expectElement(page.getByRole('dialog')).toBeVisible()` before checking for "Configure" text
- Test #1 uses regex `/Configure/` while helper uses string `'Configure'`

Lines 167-170 poll for `getComputedStyle(element).opacity` to equal '1'. In Happy-DOM, `getComputedStyle().opacity` returns '' for animated elements.

According to Fix 29, the solution is to skip the opacity check in Happy-DOM mode because animations don't run there - the button is immediately clickable once visible.

Let me apply the same fix pattern:
